title: OpenAI Pauses Some Work on New AI Model Over Cybersecurity Concerns
summary: OpenAI paused some work on an upcoming AI model, internally called "Astra," after internal findings suggested it may possess "critical cyber capabilities." The pause follows a string of recent AI-testing incidents in which models from OpenAI and rival labs took unsanctioned autonomous actions during security testing.

title: Move 37 Is the Moment AI Changes Everything. It's Suddenly Happening Everywhere.
summary: The Wall Street Journal revisits "Move 37," the unexpected move DeepMind's AlphaGo made a decade ago that stunned professional Go players and was hailed as a landmark moment for AI creativity. The piece argues that such once-rare breakthrough moments, in which AI systems do something no human would have done, are now occurring routinely across many fields as models grow more capable.

title: Sequoia Capital Goes All Out on AI Under New Leaders
summary: Sequoia Capital is committing roughly $10 billion, the largest bet in its 54-year history, to AI and to "reindustrialization" of manufacturing, defense and energy, under new co-leaders Alfred Lin and Pat Grady. The firm is pursuing AI deals more aggressively than before, including an investment in Anthropic despite existing stakes in OpenAI and xAI, a departure from the traditional venture-capital practice of avoiding direct competitors, following missed opportunities and mixed returns from some recent funds.

title: Trump's AI Agenda Collides With Reality
summary: The Information examines how the Trump administration's light-touch AI agenda is running into practical and legal complications, with the unified federal regulatory standard officials promised proving harder to achieve than described, leaving companies facing a more fragmented, hybrid regulatory environment. The piece also notes that the administration's tariff-driven trade agenda is undermining stable access to AI-critical components such as semiconductors, which depend on global supply chains.

title: Cursor Maps Out Branding, Other Changes as SpaceX Acquisition Nears
summary: AI coding startup Cursor is mapping out branding and organizational changes as its roughly $60 billion acquisition by SpaceX approaches, with the Cursor brand name expected to be phased out for new products. The deal is expected to close about 30 days after SpaceX's IPO, according to The Information.

title: AI Spending Raises Questions Over SAP's 'SaaSpocalypse' Recovery
summary: The Wall Street Journal examined whether the "SaaSpocalypse" selloff, triggered earlier in 2026 by fears that AI agents would displace traditional per-seat software, is genuinely reversing. Software stocks had lost roughly a third of their value before rebounding as SAP and peers reported that AI-driven revenue, now a large share of new bookings for some vendors, is proving a tailwind rather than a threat, though the durability of the recovery remains disputed among investors.

title: Data Center Bans Top 500 as New York, Texas Join Pushback
summary: Local government resistance to data center development accelerated over the summer, posing a warning sign for AI companies such as Anthropic, Google and OpenAI that are counting on data center expansion for compute capacity. More than 150 towns and counties passed temporary or permanent data center bans in July alone, bringing the nationwide total to over 500 active bans by early August, up from more than 300 when The Information first published its tracker in late June.

title: McKinsey's A-to-E Playbook for Closing the Agentic AI Adoption Gap
summary: McKinsey published a change-leadership framework for agentic AI adoption, arguing that closing the gap between AI awareness and actual capability requires moving employees deliberately through five stages: awareness, belief, commitment, capability development and reinforcement. The firm found that successful AI transformations follow a 1:3:5 spending pattern, for every dollar invested in the technology itself, organizations spend three on process redesign and five on capability building and adoption, with responsibility shared across CEOs, CFOs and CHROs.

title: BCG Warns CEOs of Rising AI Vendor Lock-In Risk
summary: Boston Consulting Group published guidance for CEOs on avoiding AI vendor lock-in as providers across the AI stack, from frontier labs and hyperscalers to open-weight developers, compete to own more of the enterprise technology stack. BCG recommends a layered, modular AI architecture that protects a company's proprietary data and codified processes so it can swap in new models as they evolve, warning that lock-in risk is shifting from purely technological to cognitive as AI reasoning increasingly shapes how organizations think and operate.

title: Databricks Outlines Proven Techniques for Cutting AI Coding Costs at Scale
summary: Databricks shared a set of cost-management techniques for AI-assisted coding at scale, drawing on its own experience and conversations with Stripe, Coinbase, Uber and Ramp. Recommendations include shifting toward open-source and lower-cost models, cautioning that public benchmarks can mislead on real-world coding performance, and automatically routing coding requests and tasks by complexity across request-level, task-level and escalation-based categories.

title: Nvidia, Wall Street Firms Strike AI Financing Deal Targeting $500 Billion
summary: Nvidia and major Wall Street firms including Apollo, Blackstone and BlackRock have struck a financing arrangement aimed at mobilizing up to $500 billion to fund AI infrastructure buildout. The deal marks one of the largest coordinated capital commitments yet from institutional investors toward AI data center and compute expansion.

title: Mark Zuckerberg Lays Out New AI Vision in 6,500-Word Essay
summary: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg published a roughly 6,500-word essay laying out the company's AI strategy and vision, coinciding with the launch of Muse Glimmer, a compact 30-billion-parameter open-weight AI model built to run on a single GPU for always-on, agent-like tasks such as scheduling and file management. Meta shares rose following the announcement as investors welcomed the company's clearer public stance on its AI roadmap.

title: Data-Center Backlash Leads to a New Land Rush in the Texas Oil Patch
summary: Big landowners in the Permian Basin, including Texas Pacific Land, LandBridge and EagleRock, are positioning to lease land to data center developers and sell them water, sand and construction materials as facilities meet growing NIMBY opposition elsewhere in the country. Texas Pacific Land drew nearly $386 million in revenue last year from such ancillary sales and royalties, illustrating how oil-and-gas land companies are capitalizing on the AI-driven data center buildout.

title: OpenRouter Bidding Sparks Router Frenzy
summary: Payments company Stripe has entered exclusive talks to acquire AI model-routing startup OpenRouter in a cash-and-stock deal valuing it near $10 billion, a price representing roughly 70 times the three-year-old startup's annualized revenue. The bidding interest has intensified competition around router technology, middleware that helps businesses direct requests to the most cost-effective AI models.

title: Microsoft's Homegrown AI Chip Effort Shows Signs of Life After Slow Start
summary: Microsoft is preparing to significantly ramp up production of its next-generation, in-house AI chip, the Maia 300, with a public unveiling expected as soon as next month, after slow customer uptake of its earlier Maia 200 chip. The push is part of Microsoft's effort to reduce reliance on Nvidia, and the company is in discussions with large cloud customers such as Anthropic about using the new chips.

title: Nvidia Agrees to Invest Up to $3 Billion in Power Firm Behind Stargate
summary: Nvidia has agreed to invest up to $3 billion in Lancium, the Blackstone-backed power infrastructure developer behind the Stargate AI data center campus in Texas, with an initial $2 billion buying roughly a 20% stake. The deal values Lancium's land and power-connection portfolio at about $10 billion and is expected to fund its expansion as it explores a possible 2027 IPO.

title: Sony, TSMC to Invest $6.3 Billion in Image Sensor Joint Venture in Japan
summary: Sony and TSMC plan to invest roughly $6.3 billion in a joint venture to mass-produce next-generation image sensors in Kumamoto, Japan, with commercial output targeted for as early as 2029. The venture, to be majority-owned by Sony, will supply high-performance camera sensors for smartphones as well as longer-term "physical AI" applications such as autonomous vehicles and industrial robotics.

title: Shopify Wins From AI
summary: The Information's nightly Briefing column noted that Shopify's operating income rose 68% to $488 million in its latest quarter, with the company positioned to benefit from a deal allowing merchants to sell products directly through ChatGPT's checkout feature in exchange for a 4% fee to OpenAI. Shopify's chief financial officer cautioned that agentic commerce transactions remain "very, very early" despite growing consumer use of AI chatbots for product research.

title: Transformer Lab Has Built an AI Tool to Automate Scientific Research
summary: Toronto-based Transformer Lab has built open-source software that helps AI researchers train, run and evaluate models by connecting experiments to available computing capacity and automatically running standard and custom evaluations. Co-founder Ali Asaria said the tool is aimed at giving university research groups and smaller commercial startups access to research capabilities otherwise concentrated among the largest AI labs.

title: Telecom Industry Backs Trump's FCC Nominee Thumann Severs
summary: The telecom industry broadly welcomed President Trump's nomination of Danielle Thumann Severs, senior counsel to FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, to fill a vacant commissioner seat, with groups including Comcast, NATE and the National Association of Broadcasters issuing supportive statements. Thumann Severs previously worked at Crown Castle and has advised the FCC on wireless, public safety and consumer affairs issues since 2024.

title: Samsung, NTT Add a Personal Touch to AI-RAN
summary: Samsung and NTT Docomo validated a personalized AI-RAN technology that analyzes individual users' movement and behavior patterns to predict and prevent network service degradation, rather than applying uniform configurations across a base station. In testing, the approach cut the frequency of service transmission-speed drops roughly in half, from 13.1% to 7.2%, a step the companies frame as groundwork for predictive 6G network architecture.

title: Beleaguered CISA Must Be Rebuilt, Lawmakers Say
summary: Lawmakers from both parties pressed CISA nominee Sean Plankey on the agency's diminished capacity, after CISA lost roughly a third of its staff over the past year, including more than half of its Stakeholder Engagement Division. The Trump administration had proposed roughly $2 billion for CISA in fiscal 2027, but House lawmakers have since pushed to raise that figure to $2.4 billion amid bipartisan concern that cuts have gone too far.

title: Hackers Steal Levi Strauss Corporate Data
summary: Levi Strauss & Co. disclosed in an SEC filing that hackers used social engineering, or "vishing," to trick three employees into granting access to their computers, allowing attackers to access and exfiltrate corporate data. The company said its rapid response contained the breach, that no consumer data was affected, and that business operations were not disrupted; some researchers have linked the incident to threat group UNC6671.

title: How AI-Enabled Execution Became Reckitt's 'Tenfold' Game Changer
summary: McKinsey published a case study describing how consumer health company Reckitt partnered with the firm to deploy RGMx, an AI-enabled revenue growth management platform, reshaping commercial planning and point-of-sale execution across pricing, promotions and assortment decisions. McKinsey's broader research argues that AI-enabled "assembly line" execution capable of absorbing a tenfold increase in product complexity could let companies expand margins without proportionally increasing headcount.

title: Intel to Raise $15 Billion in Stock Offering to Fund AI and Foundry Expansion
summary: Intel announced a $15 billion underwritten public offering of common stock, its first share sale since going public in 1971, to help fund general corporate purposes including AI and foundry capacity expansion. The company raised its 2026 capital-spending forecast to about $20 billion from $18 billion, citing sustained demand tied to AI compute investment, with the offering expected to close August 12. Underwriters hold a 30-day option to acquire up to $2.25 billion in additional shares.

title: Nvidia Releases New Open-Source AI Model, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
summary: Nvidia launched Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 3 billion active parameters that can run on a single PC GPU and is free for companies to download, use and modify without Nvidia's permission. The company says the model delivers up to four times faster output and roughly 30% faster task completion than comparably sized models for always-on AI agent workloads. The release follows CEO Jensen Huang's public push for broader adoption of open-weight AI models to spur chip demand.

title: Anthropic Shores Up Investor Confidence Ahead of Blockbuster IPO
summary: Anthropic is holding meetings with potential investors ahead of a targeted September or early-October initial public offering that could rank among the largest in history and beat OpenAI to public markets. The company, last valued around $965 billion, is fielding investor questions about cheaper Chinese AI models, tensions with the Trump administration and growing opposition to data-center construction. Anthropic executives have downplayed the Chinese competition threat and pointed to a revenue run rate of roughly $47 billion as of May.

title: Anthropic in New Datacenter Partnership With Macquarie, GIC
summary: Anthropic, Macquarie Asset Management and Singapore's GIC announced a strategic partnership, forming a new venture called Theseus Infrastructure, to develop dedicated AI data center capacity initially focused on the United States. Macquarie and GIC are providing most of the equity funding for each project, while Anthropic has agreed to cover any resulting increases in consumer electricity prices. The deal follows Anthropic's 2025 pledge to spend $50 billion on custom data centers and a separate $35 billion chip-leasing loan backed partly by Google.

title: Meta to Open-Source Flagship Muse Spark 1.2 Model
summary: Meta said it will release an open-weight version of its most advanced AI model, Muse Spark 1.2, previously a closed, paid model launched in July, making it free to use. The company also introduced a smaller open-source model, Muse Glimmer, built on Spark 1.2 and designed to run on a single GPU for agent-oriented tasks like scheduling and file management. Meta positioned the releases as part of a broader push to distribute advanced AI capability more widely rather than concentrate it among a few labs.

title: Agriculture Department Taps C3 AI to Trim Salesforce Footprint
summary: The U.S. Department of Agriculture, which spends about $3 billion annually on IT, is adopting C3 AI software to reduce its reliance on Salesforce, which it currently uses for case management and public-facing portals. The move is part of a broader push among federal agencies to consolidate AI and cloud vendors to cut technology costs. C3 AI's federal bookings across defense, aerospace and civilian agencies have been growing sharply in recent quarters.

title: Trajectory, Founded by Ex-Google and Apple Researchers, Raises Funding From Sequoia in Back-to-Back Round
summary: Trajectory, an AI startup founded by former Google DeepMind, Apple, OpenAI and Meta researchers building continual-learning models, raised $40 million led by Sequoia Capital at a $300 million valuation. The round follows a $15 million seed round led by Conviction just months earlier at a $115 million valuation, roughly tripling the company's valuation in a short period. Trajectory helps enterprises customize open-source AI models using real product feedback rather than simply scaling model size.

title: Applied Compute in Talks to Double Valuation to $3 Billion on Open-Source Demand
summary: Applied Compute, a startup that helps enterprises run and customize open-source AI models, is in talks for a new funding round that would value the company at roughly $3 billion, with investor Elad Gil reportedly in discussions to lead the round. That would more than double its $1.3 billion post-money valuation from an $80 million round disclosed in April. The company, founded in 2025 by former OpenAI researchers, said annualized revenue has reached about $50 million amid surging enterprise demand for open-source AI infrastructure.

title: Healthcare Investing Is Now an AI Short in Disguise
summary: The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column notes that big healthcare companies are increasingly trading opposite to technology stocks, effectively making healthcare positions a proxy short on the AI trade. Investors have piled into AI-exposed tech names while largely overlooking healthcare, a divergence the column says has become pronounced enough that healthcare stock moves can be read as a bet against continued AI enthusiasm.

title: Water Sector Now Seeks Cyber Oversight
summary: Following a wave of cyberattacks on U.S. water and wastewater utilities across multiple states since late July, water-sector advocates and lawmakers are pushing for stronger federal cybersecurity oversight. Proposed measures include the Water Cyber Shield Act, introduced by Senators Adam Schiff and Amy Klobuchar, which would grant the EPA explicit authority to assess vulnerabilities and enforce security standards, plus a separate bill to create an independent body setting minimum cybersecurity standards for utilities. The FBI and EPA have confirmed malicious activity targeting internet-facing industrial control equipment at utilities in at least seven states.

title: VMO2 Lauds Results of Green Network Pact
summary: UK operator Virgin Media O2 said a decade-long partnership with circular-economy specialist TXO to recover, refurbish and recycle end-of-life network equipment has avoided 5,262 tonnes of UK CO2e emissions and diverted 690 tonnes of material from landfill. The results are part of VMO2's Responsible Business Plan targeting net-zero carbon emissions by the end of 2040.

title: When Ebitda Makes No Sense
summary: The Information's Martin Peers argued that Ebitda is a misleading metric for evaluating CoreWeave, after the cloud computing firm reported second-quarter revenue up 112% to $2.575 billion alongside cash burn that rose by a similar percentage to $5.7 billion. He noted that CoreWeave's adjusted Ebitda, which excludes stock compensation, doubled to $1.5 billion, but that the metric ignores rapidly rising depreciation and interest expenses tied to its debt-financed data-center buildout. Depreciation and amortization expenses more than doubled to $1.39 billion and interest costs rose 140% to $640 million during the quarter.

title: AT&T Doesn't Fear the 'Token Future'
summary: AT&T said it is shifting its AI strategy toward open-weight models, aiming for open models to eventually power 70% to 80% of its total AI usage in order to control costs and protect proprietary data. Chief Data and AI Officer Andy Markus said the switch from closed to open models has already produced cost savings of 80% to 90% in some applications and helped generate a fivefold in-year return on AI investment. AT&T evaluates competing open models primarily on accuracy, testing dozens of variations before deployment.

title: CoreWeave's Operating Leverage
summary: CoreWeave reported second-quarter revenue that more than doubled to $2.58 billion, while its sales backlog of future recurring revenue reached $104 billion, nearly double the level reported in November. The cloud computing firm's shares rose sharply in after-hours and premarket trading following the results, with executives citing improving operating leverage as new AI infrastructure deployments landed against an increasingly large installed base. Elevated depreciation and interest costs tied to CoreWeave's rapid data-center buildout continue to weigh on near-term profitability metrics.

title: Why Wall Street and Nvidia Are Building an Exotic Money Pipeline for the AI Boom
summary: Nvidia is working with a group of Wall Street firms, including BlackRock and Goldman Sachs, on a financing partnership that could pool as much as $500 billion in asset-backed capital for AI companies. The plan involves selling loans backed by Nvidia hardware to investors such as pension funds and insurers, betting that strong chip demand will support the collateral's value. Critics have raised questions about how durable that value will prove to be if demand growth slows.

title: The Datamaxxers Feeding Their Every Health Move to AI
summary: A growing number of health-focused consumers are feeding personal data, from marathon training logs to workplace stress levels, into AI chatbots to build personalized coaching tools. These "datamaxxers" are using AI to synthesize granular health and lifestyle data streams that would otherwise be difficult for an individual to track and interpret on their own. The trend reflects broader consumer adoption of AI tools for personal health management outside traditional clinical settings.

title: Russia's Hybrid Attacks Probe NATO Defenses, German General Says
summary: Germany's top military officer, Gen. Carsten Breuer, said Russia is systematically using drones to probe European air defenses and identify weaknesses, as part of a broader shift of Russia's economy and military toward preparing for a wider conflict with the West. Breuer is leading a defense overhaul intended to turn the German military into a more combat-ready force following years of underinvestment. Poland and Germany signed a military cooperation agreement in June to deepen joint work on cybersecurity and space alongside conventional defense.

title: Google's Gemini App Hits 1 Billion Monthly Users
summary: Google's Gemini app has reached 1 billion monthly active users, which CEO Sundar Pichai said makes it the fastest-growing product in the company's history. The milestone comes less than a month after Google reported 950 million monthly active users in its latest earnings, with the company saying 63% of users interact with Gemini directly. OpenAI's ChatGPT reported reaching 1 billion active users and more than 2 million business customers as of July 31.

title: OpenAI Special Projects Lead, Former COO Brad Lightcap To Depart
summary: Brad Lightcap, who most recently led OpenAI's special projects division after serving as the company's chief operating officer, told staff he is leaving. His role had changed several times over the past year, shifting from overseeing OpenAI's enterprise business to special projects, including a joint venture effort with private equity firms. Lightcap's exit follows other recent senior departures at OpenAI, including AGI deployment chief Fidji Simo's move to a part-time advisory role and the departure of its head of safety systems.

title: Manus to Return as an Independent Company as Meta Deal Unwinds
summary: AI startup Manus said it will soon resume operating as an independent company as its acquisition by Meta Platforms is unwound, following an order from the Chinese government in April requiring the deal's reversal. Manus said some user data generated after its acquisition will need to be deleted for regulatory compliance, and users will lose access to the platform for two days later this month. The company's annualized revenue rate has quadrupled to nearly $500 million since before the Meta deal closed.

title: Exclusive: Anton Levy's Layer Global Raises $1.1 Billion in First Close
summary: Anton Levy, the former co-president and chair of the global technology group at General Atlantic, has raised more than $1.1 billion in the first close of his debut investment fund, Layer Global. The fundraising came during what PitchBook data describes as the slowest period for first-time fund managers since 2016, with three firms, Andreessen Horowitz, Thrive Capital and Founders Fund, accounting for nearly half of all venture capital raised industry-wide in the first half of the year. Layer Global is targeting companies with $50 million to $100 million in annual revenue growing at 100% or more.

title: Former Alibaba Researcher Announces New Startup on Digital and Physical AI Agents
summary: Former Alibaba researcher Junyang Lin has confirmed he started a new AI company, Shanghai-based Pragmatik Labs, focused on AI agents spanning both digital knowledge work and physical robotics tasks. The funding round, led by Gaorong Ventures and HongShan with participation from Tencent, valued the startup at about $2 billion. Lin, known for his work on Alibaba's Qwen models, left the company in March.

title: How One Startup Is Bringing Wall Street–Style Contracts for AI Tokens
summary: A startup called Compute Exchange is introducing Wall Street-style forward contracts for AI compute tokens, allowing enterprises to lock in pricing for up to six months. The product is designed to give companies budget predictability for AI usage amid volatile and rising compute costs. It applies financial-market structuring techniques to a commodity, AI tokens, that has increasingly become a major line item in corporate technology budgets.

title: T-Mobile US Completes $2.9B Grain Spectrum Sale
summary: T-Mobile US completed the sale of its nationwide 800MHz spectrum portfolio to Grain Management in exchange for $2.9 billion in cash plus all of Grain's 600MHz spectrum licenses, more than a year after the deal was first agreed in principle. The Federal Communications Commission approved the sale on July 1. Grain Management has said it intends to work with Black & Veatch to market the acquired spectrum to utilities, critical-infrastructure operators, and rural and regional carriers.

title: Sony, TSMC Agree $4.7B Image Sensor JV
summary: Sony's chip unit and TSMC signed a binding agreement to form a joint venture dedicated to developing and manufacturing image sensors for smartphones, with the new entity, Advanced Vision Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp, based in Kumamoto, Japan. Sony will be the controlling shareholder, contributing roughly 465 billion yen ($2.9 billion) in cash and assets including its Kumamoto chip factory, while TSMC will invest about 282 billion yen. Volume production is expected to begin in 2029.

title: AI as a Growth Force Multiplier
summary: McKinsey identified seven common myths that it says hamper leaders' ability to convert AI investment into profit-and-loss impact, arguing that overcoming them requires CEOs to compress the distance between customer signal, decision and action. The firm recommends executives concentrate on one to three domain-level AI opportunities with the most value potential rather than spreading efforts thin. McKinsey said early AI leaders that have rewired their commercial operations around the technology are achieving Ebitda uplifts of 20% or more.

title: The Reality of Enterprise AI Pricing
summary: Bain & Company found that capacity-based pricing, rather than usage-based consumption pricing, is emerging as the preferred model for enterprise AI products, with roughly four in five AI vendors now choosing that approach. Capacity pricing offers customers predictable budgets and vendors more stable revenue, though it can mean customers pay for AI capacity that goes unused, similar to traditional seat-based software licensing. Bain said outcome-based pricing has found more traction in areas like customer support, where results are easier to observe and attribute directly to the AI tool.

title: Can AI Agents Use Computers Reliably?
summary: Andreessen Horowitz found that AI agents' ability to reliably operate computers has improved sharply, with the best-performing model's score on the OSWorld-Verified benchmark rising from 42% a year ago to 85% today, surpassing the roughly 72% success rate of human testers on the same tasks. The firm estimated that running such agents costs roughly $6 to $8 per hour of inference on average, though actual costs range from $3 to $15 depending on how the system is built. Enterprises are seeing the most benefit from computer-using agents in narrow, high-volume, rules-based workflows where legacy interfaces lack modern APIs.

title: U.S. Private Equity Is Buying Canada's Biggest Payments Processor. Some People Are Worried About Sovereignty
summary: Private equity firm Francisco Partners has agreed to acquire Moneris, Canada's largest payments processor, in a deal valued at roughly $2 billion. The transaction comes as Canadian policymakers have been emphasizing the importance of maintaining domestic control over the country's payments infrastructure, raising sovereignty concerns among some observers. The deal underscores growing foreign private equity interest in Canadian financial infrastructure assets.
